summary: No held thesis is broken by evidence in the files. Today's four sales (VOO, VTI, FAST, EXEL) rested on the tripped shared SPY stop, met market-condition clauses and the lost Health Care tilt, not on any fundamental deterioration. FAST and EXEL left the book with their screen-level quality intact, so they can come back as candidates once the regime filter and the 12-20 wash windows allow. Of the 10 remaining positions none is TRIPPED. SAM (3.26% above its $201 stop after -5.0% today) and INCY (4.2% above $110) are closest, but both moves are price, and price alone does not break a thesis. About 42% of equity is cash because the regime filter idles it.
update: Holding-by-holding check against close.json. (1) SAM is the weakest fundamental case still held. Its F8 and gp_sector_pct 0.945 come from FY2025 numbers that predate the 2026 quarters, net income ($108M) is thin, and founder Jim Koch hands the CEO role to COO Phil Hodges on 11-23 (8-K 5.02). The PM calls this a planned internal succession with no guidance change, which is a fair reading. It is a reason to watch, not a broken thesis. The clause 'the fundamentals screen drops SAM from the menu' needs checking against tomorrow's menu. (2) IDXX: the PM restated it today under L8 to rest on quality (F8, gp_sector_pct 0.942, CFO $1,181.8M vs NI $1,059.5M) and the 11-02 beat-and-raise. That is the right basis. The over $27M of executive selling is sentiment and touches no clause. It is still the named next trim candidate, on beta and sector grounds, not fundamental ones. (3) INCY: CFO $1,413.5M against NI $1,286.7M still backs earnings. The MAESTRA-3 drop (8-K 8.01, guidance kept) and two small insider sales are pipeline and sentiment items, not a failed pivotal trial, so the clause is untripped. (4) MSCI: fails leverage_not_up and has done so since purchase. With MCO gone, that is now a single-name concern, not a sleeve one; still low severity. (5) DPZ (L3): its Staples rank is still a wholesale-groceries SIC artifact, and the case rests on absolute quality (F8, CFO $792M vs NI $602M). By SIC label, DPZ (11.8%) plus WMT, KR and SAM (about 16.5% by bucket) is about 28% of equity in one label, and that is now the largest exposure in a 58%-invested book. (6) L6 stale text, which the PM should fix through thesis_updates: DPZ still stores a return figure ('-$0.62 on this position in a 10% market drop'), 'while the tape rotates away from tech' and 'No earnings inside 5 trading days' from 10-20. VRSN still stores the 10-26 add rationale ('chases a 3.6% gain') and the line that its data predates the Q3 print. CARG's 'Rank 2 on fundamentals' is a dated rank. (7) TLT has no fundamentals. Its $76.30 stop is stored against the $80.35 reference close and should be restated from the $80.75 fill at the next run (L6). (8) WMT's restated XLP clause sits close: XLP 21d is +3.16% against the +3% line, so it is the stored condition nearest to tripping on a non-price test. Lessons applied: L3 (the DPZ label and the Staples label stack), L6 (stale and return-figure text) and L8 (IDXX and INCY restated off the lost sector tilt). None conflicted with today's evidence. learning.json has no graded fundamentals-analyst calls yet.
